title: codex exec in an untrusted directory ignores project config and MCP servers even with --sandbox workspace-write
symptoms: MCP servers defined in the project's .codex/config.toml are not started under codex exec
Project-level settings have no effect in codex exec after upgrading to 0.169.0
Passing --sandbox workspace-write does not change which project config is loaded
cause: As of 0.169.0, codex exec keeps project configuration and MCP servers disabled in directories that are not trusted. Choosing a sandbox mode no longer implies trust, so a script that relied on workspace-write to pick up project config now runs without it.
fix: Mark the project as trusted explicitly by passing --trust to codex exec or codex review, which saves project trust. Alternatively trust the directory once in an interactive session before running automation.
affected: Codex CLI 0.169.0 and later, for codex exec and codex review in directories not yet trusted
